really?? this is the sequel to clone drone in the danger zone??? im sorry but this simply was not fun both combat and storywise- spoilers ahead the game doesnt do a great job of explaining a whole lot other than "you're in a loop where you fight and you can defeat people" and half of the game felt like it was talking and story so i was really hoping that part would be good when it just felt like filler. genuinely i felt like i was just playing a story game :/ then there's the actual combat. it felt fun for 5 minutes then it was just clunky and boring, and this was the part i was excited for. veeeery lackluster amount of weapons and most just werent fun to use anyways. i guess the gloves were cool? i liked combining them. they felt really gimmicky though and i often didn't see myself using them in fights anyways except for cheese kills. speaking of cheese kills, the difficulty was atrociously easy... i didnt need cheese kills because enemies had huge windups that left everything exposed. teleporting was op. walking was just slow but thats only fair because theres a "dash" that lets you move at normal speed but even that let you easily kill stuff. great, normal enemies are basically nonexistant- but the bosses are surely difficult and fun, right? no. they're arguably worse than normal enemies. you can walk up to half of them and just kill them. i spent around 5x longer waiting for a new clone of them to come out than actually fighting them. final boss was the exact same way. all of that, but surely theres atleast a way to turn my brain off and infinitely play levels or maybe even just a satisfying practice arena right? nope, at this point in time there is no infinite mode and no training grounds. there arent even physics for throwing stuff. seriously??? i cant even throw weapons??? i dont even know, im just frustrated that such a good first game has such an unfun sequel. i really tried to enjoy this and i kind of did for the first hour but after that it was just walking up to enemies that dont pose a real threat, getting through levels (waiting between levels took as long as the levels themselves, and i have a good computer), occasionally fighting bosses, and then listening to people talk. i was atleast hoping for the commentator bots to be there as much as in the original D: i dont really expect to get a refund since its past the 2 hour mark, which is unfortunate because i spent upwards of 2 hours waiting for it to get more fun. personally, i suggest trying the game- if you dont like it after 30-60 mniutes, then refund because it really doesn't change a ton. ill probably consider buying it again a year from now assuming it gets updated but at its current state i really just can't recommend it. sorry doborog </3

old review: extremely fun game, except for the fact that: 1. The combat is extremely inconsistent, sometimes, I can take multiple hits from robots without dying, and being able to just flail my arms around, waiting for them to walk into my sword and inevitably die. And at other times, a graze to my head or chest kills me instantly, while almost a full cut through my opponents stomach or a shallow stab to their head (more on that later) leaves them completely fine and unfazed. Sometimes, I can just completely run through my opponents blades without a scratch, and at other times I "parry" my opponents attack, but their sword goes through mine(??). 2. Every weapon except for the small sword suck. The two handed longswords or greatswords are extremely janky in the sense that they do not go where you control, want or expect them to go which leads to unprecise cuts and sometimes just blatantly missing the enemy or a parry. I suggest you make the offhand have significantly less control of the blade's orientation compared to your dominant hand, in order to prevent this. Stabbing in this game really sucks, i tried using the rapier at one point. Although it was cool that the blade wobbles, the stabbing in this game is atrociously horrid. A full thrust/lunge with the rapier usually just leaves a shallow dent in the robots, but in the off-chance that it completely penetrates, the enemies are completely fine as only cuts/dismemberment does actual damage in this game. I suggest that you should add something similar as to vital organs (such as a cpu or energy cell) so that stabbing said organs would actually affect the enemies. Axes (including the glaive which also has the issues of the aforementioned stabbing) are not good in this game, you trade range, stabs and cutting surface for what exactly? Irl, axes had much higher penetration and chopping power than other available weapons, meaning you could sometimes, for example, cut/chop through shields or armour, which would also be mildly nifty in this game if these features were implemented (perhaps along with the ability to cut through hilts). I assume scythes would be decent in this game, I havent tried them. They have pretty good range and an admirably large blade, and can also attack from behind (probably risky though). And I bet the ai is dumb enough to just walk into the blade. Also, make it so that you are able to cut through bows. 3. The ai is pretty dumb, in my opinion. They can't riposte, hell they cant even parry. All they do is attack you very a veeeeery long windup which gives you a big amount of time to react and place your blade accordingly. The ai in this game is also very unpredictable, for example: at first it might seem like they are striking you from the upper right, but then almost like they are teleporting, suddenly the blade comes from somewhere else slicing you in half. And dont get me started on when you cut of the arm of a robot wielding a two-handed weapon. If I were to be killed by a robot parrying my attack and then riposting, it would be much more satisfying and less frustrating to die by that, then to die by jank. I hope to the person reading this takes my review as criticism, and not hate. I love the concept and the dynamic slicing of this game, and sometimes this game is very fun to play. update: i bought this game once more as it seems as the dev(s) have fixed some of the issues i stated in this review, and they did. most of the two-handed weapons actually feel pretty good to use now (except the scythe, i hate its handling), but the general consistency of the combat is still inconsistent, enemies can still "power through" structured parries, they still "lob" weapons around at awkward angles (which is more of a problem of the omni-edge of most weapons that i'm just not used to i can admit) and it still seems that any light graze against the head or torso warrants an instant kill to the player while it does nothing to enemies, and i think i found another issue being that the player camera is slightly behind the head? also if you're buying this game solely (or if it is a big part of your decision), don't bother. the inner voice thing is seriously insufferable and i hope we get an option to disable it in the future.

作为前作Clone Drone in the Danger Zone的老玩家而言，这个VR版真是意料之中的惊喜。 很早之前我就“预言”过这游戏出个VR版本会很赞，实际游玩后的体验虽然和预期有些出入，但还是很爽的。 虽然说激光剑的手感基本上砍啥都是切黄油，但这游戏有一个其他剑斗游戏都没有的独特爽感：拼刀角力！在你的剑和对方的武器格挡相撞的时候，可以实现非常动漫感的拼刀场面，一些现实里的剑术在这种机制下也开始有用了起来，比如挑剑之类的。但部分武器的手感做的很鸡肋，尤其是长柄武器，算是VR剑斗的通病。 玩法方面，竞技场型Rougelike，可以自由拾取场上和敌人掉落的武器，难度适中，需要不少动态视力和环境意识（小心背后偷袭），VR不耐受群体可能会玩的不太舒服。 游戏本身也有一点小剧情，而且剧情似乎和每个角色都有分支和特殊对话，每个人物的刻画都不错，配音也很棒。 目前的缺点就是没有中文字幕和翻译对于英语不熟悉的玩家来说难以游玩吧……

[h1] 人类的意识——你很强，但是不够强 [/h1] 当你的意识真的被下载到机器人身上，开启永无止境的角斗场...... 你的双手得以解放，要么双手各执利刃，要么把长枪挥舞形如吕布。有时候，你被砍下一条手臂，这也许突然激发了你的“求生本能”，突然觉醒大杀四方......或许是成为了杨过；有时候，你则掌控原力，在敌人跃向你时将其推下葬身熔岩......由此可以使出另所有机器人为之震颤的超绝招式——此刻，你很强......至少你是这么认为的。十余次将来犯敌人拦腰斩断、削做机棍甚至细细剁成臊子，将向你飞来的箭矢弹得四处迸发。你或许开始陷入无敌的虚无之中，于是，噩梦悄然而至。 敌人很聪明，至少比你认为的要聪明。也许你自诩武德充沛，亦或者本身就是耗子尾汁之徒，无论如何，你开始发现团队协作的机器人有两种行为模式——要么肆意挥砍屠刀不分敌我，像极了路人队友；要么合作无间，前者骗你招架，后者绕后千年杀，如同同室开黑......不管你是怎样的老同志，你终于还是为他们这些年轻人来偷来骗的不讲武德而不齿。 因此在人类和机器人的较量中，你永远也不知道自己能活过哪一关......如今你兴许能够理解前作的可怜人类是什么感受XD 在变强的道路上，大家都是求索者，乱拳打死一大片不是本事，在一次次死亡中得出自己不够强的结论才是道路的刚刚开始。 *避免剧透，本作含有的友情啊羁绊啊什么的不做展开

Clone Drone in the Hyperdome has a state of the art melee system that decimates VR melee competitors like Blade & Sorcery, though fails HORRIBLY in balance. As soon as you get a single upgrade, especially ranged upgrades, the game effectively becomes cooldown management. There's no point in engaging with the melee system if you can just point, press trigger, and wait a few times. Even if you ignore the upgrades, the Enemy AI is pretty incapable of dodging and is incapable of hurting crouched players. Even just having a longer weapon invalidates the AI. The bossfights further exemplify this problem, especially with the fact that you can literally just teleport to their spawn location and insta-kill them. Without fail. I'll probably update this review after the 'Skyscrapper' update to see if there's any improvements/if the endless mode provides proper challenge.

Theres alot of VR games that do weapon melee combat and alot of them do it very well but CDITH does it the best. CDITH advances the genre by adding binding, a mechanic where you can clash weapons and they may stick together so you can face off with your opponent like two jedis in a sabre clash. this allows you to take control of your enemies weapon and pull off staggering techniques. CDITH has obviously been studying its genre, it uses physics up to the point where it detracts from the game. you can punch and push enemies around by they will always keep their feet planted which makes combat always a threat. you can be killed in one blow and so can the enemies. you can lose arms and legs and you just have to made do without. you can parry arrows out of the air, trick your enemies into swinging and killing their friends, duck underneath weapons and cut right through them. If you want to master the sword, no other game will give you the options of skill expression like CDITH. buy it if you love the melee genre, its worth twice the price of admission

This game took me by surprise! The screen shots and videos don't do this one justice for how good this game actually is to play in VR! I'm not always a huge fan of the voxel style, but the developers have worked some magic in this one, making it so you can break off little parts of the character's body by striking them with a variety of weapons and power ups, adding to the gameplay style, giving you limitless ways to cut through the robots. With a full on story mode, filled with characters that have awesome dialogue voiced by real actors, this one had me hooked from the start, constantly giving me high energy with the epic original soundtrack while working my way through the crash loop, diving into randomly generated levels, adding constant variety to the gameplay and unlocking all the characters while making my way to the end end...but then it wasn't the end. Once complete with the main story mode, a new area unlocks called the skyscrapper, and this is an awesome rogue lite mode, where you need to fight through random waves of enemies, floor by floor, with each floor getting harder and harder, but you are aided by power ups every few levels and many weapons to fight with to aid you on your journey, ascending higher through the Giant building, trying to beat your previous score! This game has some amazing features, including haptic support for some Haptic vest brands, and definitely not one to pass on if you enjoy fast-paced, action packed VR combat!
